the temporal dynamics of avian malaria prevalence in mosquitoes is complex and that further research is required to better understand the underlying factors and processes involved.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that the prevalence and composition of the Plasmodium parasite community in Culex pipens mosquitoes was dynamic, and that the community was composed of multiple lineages, including P. relicitum (SGS lineages) and P. vaughanii (lineage SYT05).
we found a high prevalence of Plasmodia in Cx pipiens, with a seasonal variation in the relative abundance of different Plasmodia species.
we have demonstrated that mosquito abundance, avian malaria prevalence, and Plasmodia lineage composition are not static but vary over time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal dynamics of the mosquito population, the mosquito-parasite interactions and the parasite community structure are tightly linked.
the time window for the analysis of mosquito-parasite dynamics is critical.
